# Summary


**Background**:
Volatile anaesthetics contribute to the environmental footprint of operating rooms.
CONTRAfluran^TM^ (ZeoSys Medical GmbH, Berlin, Germany)
passively captures sevoflurane at the anaesthesia machine exhaust port
for thermal desorption and pharmaceutical reuse.
Multicentre evidence on its capture efficiency is lacking.

**Methods**:
In this prospective, multicentre observational study,
`r n_agcs["initial"]` CONTRAfluran canisters were deployed in
`r n_ors["initial"]` operating rooms across `r n_center["initial"]` hospitals
in Germany and Austria
from `r format(lubridate::floor_date(study_period[1L], "month"), "%B %Y")`
to `r format(lubridate::floor_date(study_period[2L], "month"), "%B %Y")`.
Each operating room received `r n_bottles_per_or` sevoflurane bottles.
Case-level data were recorded on paper case report forms.
Predictors of per-canister recapture were explored
with LASSO regression and stability selection.

**Results**:
After exclusions, `r n_agcs["final"]` canisters from
`r n_ors["final"]` operating rooms in `r n_center["final"]` hospitals
underwent thermal desorption.
They covered `r n_cases["final"]` of `r n_cases["initial"]` anaesthesia cases.
ZeoSys recovered `r round(zeosys_sevo_weight_kg, 1)` kg of sevoflurane
at a purity above `r zeosys_purity_pct`%.
This corresponds to a capture efficiency of `r round(recovery_pct_final, 1)`%
for the analysed canisters.
In LASSO regression and stability selection,
the median fresh gas flow during inhalational anaesthesia
was the only consistent predictor.
Water trap use was associated with higher recapture.

**Conclusions**:
CONTRAfluran canisters recaptured approximately
`r round(recovery_pct_final, 0)`%
of administered sevoflurane under routine clinical conditions,
consistent with prior single-centre findings.
Fresh gas flow during inhalational anaesthesia
was the main predictor of per-canister recapture.

**Keywords**:
inhalational anaesthesia; sevoflurane; vapour capture technology; capture efficiency
